key_insight: Better pretraining performance does not necessarily mean better results after fine-tuning. Beyond a sufficiently large pretraining data budget, AdamW outperforms Muon on downstream performance, despite Muon's advantage in reducing pretraining loss.
problem_solved: Determines whether Muon's pretraining advantage over AdamW carries over to downstream fine-tuning, and how that comparison changes with pretraining data scale and model size.
method: Compare Muon and AdamW in pretraining and subsequent fine-tuning.
Vary pretraining data budgets to identify when the downstream performance ranking reverses.
Examine how model size affects the optimizer comparison.
impact: Practitioners should evaluate optimizer choices using post-fine-tuning performance, not pretraining loss alone. AdamW may be the better choice at larger pretraining data budgets.
visual_elements: Crossover chart: downstream performance versus pretraining data budget, with Muon and AdamW curves.
Two-stage pipeline: pretraining → fine-tuning, highlighting that optimizer rankings can change.
Small-multiple charts comparing the optimizer gap across model sizes.
Contrasting metric cards: pretraining loss advantage versus downstream performance advantage.
paper_title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
paper_authors: Catherine Li, Jingchu Gai, Andrej Risteski, Jacob Mitchell Springer, Aditi Raghunathan
